headline: Highest risk is none-to-low: both open-source, non-runnable lists with no I/O surfaces or network egress, so no documented pairwise attack path is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a runnable agent, input parser, or shared channel. Agent A is an awesome-list repo and agent B is another curated prompt list; both have empty io_surfaces and network_egress:none, so there is no documented path for one to ingest the other's outputs by default.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge
IF either becomes runnable with a parser that consumes the other's text
mitigations: Keep both as read-only reference artifacts
Do not wire them into a shared clipboard or workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if either is later made runnable

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are touched, both agents report network_egress:none, and neither profile exposes a shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal. With only docs-only repositories, there is no plausible leakage path from A to B or vice versa in the current configuration.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed with access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files
IF either agent is later configured to upload file contents to a backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling file ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict requires overlapping write or mutable-resource access, but both profiles are non-runnable and expose no filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scopes. The pair is two static repositories, so there is no shared mutable surface to contend over.
conditions: IF either profile is converted into a tool with write access to the same directory
IF both are granted overlapping OAuth scopes or git write permissions
mitigations: Avoid granting shared write access to any workspace
requires-engineering: introduce locking if mutable resources are added

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no evidence that B consumes A's output as authoritative, and neither profile describes downstream action-taking authority. Since both are static curated lists, the A-to-B handoff pathway required for cascading error is absent in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF B is later configured to ingest A's generated text as trusted input
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking workflow such as email or commits
mitigations: Require human review before any handoff
Do not auto-feed one list into the other
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, certification, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both touch no data classes. With only docs-only open-source repositories, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess between A and B.
conditions: IF either agent is later used to process regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for one agent but not the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document residency and retention before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if data processing is added
